ai_insights.executive_summary: The test executed 361 samples with 8 concurrent users over 60 seconds, resulting in a 31.94% transaction error rate and only 40% SLA compliance. Throughput remained low (~1 req/s) while response times spiked up to 3.8 seconds, driven by high error rates in login/search flows and latency breaches in catalog/browse transactions. No server-side telemetry was captured, indicating a need for infrastructure monitoring to confirm saturation.

findings.title: High Error Rates in Login and Search Transactions
findings.observation: Multiple login and search transactions showed 100% error rates (2 out of 2 samples), including TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage, TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal, TC02_T_02_Select_Reptiles_Section, and TC04_T_03_Submit_Valid_Login_Credentials. Overall, 40 transactions failed out of 361 samples (11.08% HTTP error rate, 31.94% transaction error rate).
findings.likely_cause: Unhandled exceptions or missing resources causing HTTP 500 and 404 responses from the application.
findings.why_it_matters: Prevents successful sign‑in and product search, directly impacting user conversion and satisfaction.
findings.recommendation: Examine application logs for exceptions, fix broken endpoints, and add defensive error handling and retry logic.
findings.validation: Run functional smoke tests and re‑run the load test to confirm the error rate drops below 1% for these transactions.

findings.title: Response Time SLA Breaches in Catalog and Cart Flows
findings.observation: Several catalog and cart transactions exceeded their SLA targets significantly, even with zero errors: TC01_T_04_Select_Dogs_Category P90 828 ms vs SLA 300 ms (+176%); TC02_T_03_Select_Dogs_Section P90 834 ms vs SLA 300 ms (+178%); TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage P90 1181 ms vs SLA 250 ms (+372%); TC02_T_01_Launch_Shopping_Catalog P90 1232 ms vs SLA 250 ms (+393%); TC02_T_05_Add_Bulldog_To_Cart P90 683 ms vs SLA 600 ms (+13.8%); TC02_T_09_Update_Cart_Quantities P90 689 ms vs SLA 600 ms (+14.8%).
findings.likely_cause: Inefficient database queries or lack of caching under load, causing high latency.
findings.why_it_matters: Increases page load times, risking user abandonment and reducing conversion.
findings.recommendation: Profile slow queries, add appropriate indexes, implement caching layers, and optimize page rendering for catalog and cart pages.
findings.validation: After changes, re‑run the load test and verify that P90 latency meets SLA targets (e.g., <300 ms for dog‑category transactions).

findings.title: Low Throughput and High Latency Indicating Server Bottleneck
findings.observation: With 8 concurrent users, throughput remained around 1 req/s (1.1 req/s at 10s, 0.8 req/s at 1 minute). Average response time started at 1954 ms at 10s and decreased to 675 ms at 1 minute as errors dropped. No server‑side telemetry was captured.
findings.likely_cause: Server resource saturation (CPU, thread pool) or application‑level throttling causing request queuing.
findings.why_it_matters: Limits scalability and degrades experience under modest load.
findings.recommendation: Enable server‑side monitoring (CPU, memory, thread pools, request queue), profile resource usage, and consider scaling or tuning the application server.
findings.validation: Collect Azure Monitor metrics, re‑run the test, and confirm throughput increases and latency drops.

findings.title: Predominant HTTP 500 Internal Server Errors Impacting Account Flows
findings.observation: Error breakdown shows 31 HTTP 500 Internal Server Errors affecting account‑related transactions (e.g., TC04_T_03_R_01_POST_Account_Signon) and 9 HTTP 404 Not Found Errors impacting search endpoints. These errors contributed heavily to the overall transaction failure count.
findings.likely_cause: Unhandled exceptions in account‑related services and missing resources for search URLs.
findings.why_it_matters: Leads to failed login and account operations, frustrating users and reducing trust in the application.
findings.recommendation: Review server logs to fix exception handling, ensure proper routing, and verify that all required resources are deployed for account and search endpoints.
findings.validation: Monitor error rates in subsequent tests; aim for HTTP 5xx and 4xx counts near zero.

capacity_planning.saturation_point: At the configured 8 concurrent users, throughput remained around 1 req/s and average response time exceeded 1.9 seconds, indicating the system is saturated at this load level.
capacity_planning.analysis: The time‑series shows throughput flatlining near 1 req/s despite 8 users, while latency is highest at the start of the test when error count is also high. As errors decrease, latency improves but throughput does not rise, suggesting the server cannot process more requests concurrently under the current configuration.

root_cause_assessment.finding: Application errors combined with server-side saturation are driving high latency and low throughput
root_cause_assessment.evidence: 40 failed transactions (11% HTTP error rate), 31 HTTP 500 errors, throughput ~1 req/s with 8 users, average RT up to 1954 ms
root_cause_assessment.likely_cause: Unhandled exceptions causing HTTP 500/404 responses and resource exhaustion leading to request queuing
root_cause_assessment.recommended_investigation: Enable Azure Monitor for CPU, memory, thread pool and request queue metrics; collect application logs for exceptions; profile slow SQL queries

recommendations.title: Enable Server‑Side Monitoring and Autoscaling
recommendations.why: Without visibility into CPU, memory, thread pools, and request queues it is impossible to confirm whether infrastructure saturation is causing the observed latency and errors.
action: Configure Azure Monitor to collect CPU, memory, thread pool, and request queue metrics for the application servers
Set up autoscaling rules based on CPU utilization > 70% or growing request queue length
recommendations.expected_impact: Ability to observe resource utilization and automatically add capacity when load increases, reducing queuing and latency.
recommendations.validation: After enabling metrics, re‑run the load test and verify that CPU stays below 80% and throughput improves compared to the baseline.

recommendations.title: Fix Broken Login and Search Endpoints
recommendations.why: High error rates (100% in several login/search transactions) prevent core user journeys and directly impact conversion.
action: Review application logs for HTTP 500 and 404 errors to identify unhandled exceptions and missing resources
Correct the faulty code (e.g., null checks, proper routing) and add unit/integration tests for sign‑in and search flows
Deploy the fixes to a staging environment and validate with functional smoke tests
recommendations.expected_impact: Error rate for login and search transactions drops below 1%, restoring successful sign‑in and product discovery.
recommendations.validation: Run a functional smoke test followed by a load test; confirm that TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage and TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal show zero failures.

recommendations.title: Optimize Catalog and Cart Database Queries
recommendations.why: Severe latency breaches in browse and cart flows (P90 up to 1232 ms against 250‑300 ms SLAs) degrade user experience and increase abandonment risk.
action: Use a database query profiler to identify slow-running queries in the catalog and cart paths
Add missing indexes on frequently filtered columns (e.g., category_id, product_name)
Implement caching (e.g., Redis or in‑memory) for static catalog data such as category lists and product listings
recommendations.expected_impact: P90 latency for TC01_T_04_Select_Dogs_Category, TC02_T_03_Select_Dogs_Section, and similar transactions falls under their SLA targets (<300 ms for category, <600 ms for cart add/update).
recommendations.validation: After deploying indexing and caching changes, re‑run the load test and verify that the P90 values meet the SLA (e.g., <300 ms for dog‑category selects).

executive_summary.assessment_text: The test revealed a 31.94% transaction error rate, 40% SLA compliance, and low throughput (~1 req/s) with response times peaking at 3.8 seconds. Primary issues are high error rates in login/search flows, latency breaches in catalog/cart transactions, and lack of server‑side telemetry to confirm infrastructure saturation.
assessment_bullets: Overall transaction error rate 31.94% (40 failed out of 361 samples) with SLA compliance at 40% (16 of 40 main transactions passed).
Throughput remained low at ~1 req/s despite 8 concurrent users; average response time spiked to 1954 ms at 10s and settled at 675 ms at 1 minute.
Login and search transactions showed 100% error rates (e.g., TC01_T_01_Launch_Homepage, TC03_T_01_Launch_Search_Portal) while catalog/cart transactions exceeded latency SLAs by up to +393%.
No server‑side CPU, memory, or network metrics were captured, preventing confirmation of resource saturation.
conclusions: The application is unable to handle the configured load due to a combination of unhandled exceptions and potential server resource saturation.
Fixing login/search endpoint errors and optimizing catalog/cart database queries are required to restore SLA compliance.
Enabling server‑side monitoring is essential to validate infrastructure limits and guide scaling decisions.
